commercialResearch.note: The provider announcement says Price Feeds API plans start at 500 USD per month; current exact plan, allowance, overage, SLA, tax, cancellation, and license terms remain unverified and unapproved.

Standard onchain feeds are described as a community resource, but RPC transport, provider plan, API usage rights, support, SLA, and total cost require separate approval. No zero-cost production claim is made.

sourceEvidence.observedFact: Pyth Core documents first-party aggregated price feeds, a 400 millisecond update model, and push and pull delivery across more than 100 blockchains.
The official catalog documents distinct stable Pyth Core feed identifiers for Crypto.USDC/USD, Crypto.USDT/USD, and Crypto.PYUSD/USD.
The fetch guide documents Hermes REST, streaming, and SDK delivery, bearer-token authentication, and latest updates keyed by exact feed ID.
The published Hermes and Benchmarks limit is 10 requests per 10 seconds per IP, with a 60-second 429 penalty after exceeding it; exact authenticated-plan limits remain unverified.
The documented response shape includes integer price, absolute conf, exponent, and publish_time fields; this packet never fetched a live response.
The provider announced that Price Feeds API access requires a subscription and that plans start at 500 USD per month; exact current terms and allowances require KAN-252 review.
Pyth separately documents native-token fees for onchain price updates; onchain writes and their fees are prohibited and out of scope for this decision.
The price-feed disclaimer provides the service as-is and as-available, disclaims continuity and accuracy guarantees, and places stale checks, circuit breakers, monitoring, and testing on users.
The website terms restrict automated extraction and unauthorized API access and do not establish production API data rights for this project; exact subscription terms require Legal approval.
Chainlink documents read-only AggregatorV3 latestRoundData access, including answer and updatedAt, through an RPC endpoint; the response has no native confidence interval.
The official catalog documents the Ethereum mainnet standard USDC/USD feed and a 0.25 percent deviation trigger; exact contract and heartbeat remain pending live validation.
The official catalog documents the Ethereum mainnet standard USDT/USD feed and a 0.25 percent deviation trigger; exact contract and heartbeat remain pending live validation.
The official catalog documents the Ethereum mainnet standard PYUSD/USD feed and a 0.3 percent deviation trigger; exact contract and heartbeat remain pending live validation.
Chainlink describes aggregation across premium data providers and independent oracle nodes; overlap with Pyth publishers or underlying venues was not quantified.

Chainlink requires consumers to understand feed market, provider, and contract risks, monitor shutdown or deprecation, implement circuit breakers, and treat stablecoin exchange-rate feeds as market prices rather than guaranteed one-dollar values.
